summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Mitra Chem is the last DOE-funded lithium-iron-phosphate cathode plant left in the United States pipeline after ICL cancelled its St. Louis project in November 2025 — and, as of 12 September 2026, it has not broken ground, has published nothing on its own channels since 20 September 2024, sold USD 15.6 million of a USD 50 million round in mid-2025 with no closing on record, and now carries a plant cost the State of Michigan puts at over USD 370 million against USD 150 million of public grants. Groundbreaking is guided to early 2027 and commissioning to 2028, a year later than the 2024 guidance.

**BACKGROUND.** Mitra Future Technologies, Inc., trading as Mitra Chem, is a Delaware corporation founded in 2021 in Mountain View, California by Vivas Kumar (formerly Tesla's battery-materials supply chain and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence), Chirranjeevi Gopal and Stanford professor William Chueh. It develops lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP) cathode active material — the powder that is roughly a third of a storage cell's cost and is made almost entirely in China — using an AI-driven process-development platform it says compresses lab-to-production time by 90%. Financing per SEC Form D: a USD 20 million Series A (2021, Social Capital), a USD 60 million Series B led by GM (USD 27.05 million sold at the July 2023 filing; 'nearly USD 80 million' cumulative by March 2024 per the company) and a 2025 round of USD 49,999,996 with USD 15,599,991 sold at 9 June 2025, into which L&F Co. of Korea put USD 10 million for a reported 3.3%. The US Department of Energy obligated a USD 100 million Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains grant on 16 December 2024 for a 15,000 tonne-per-year LFP plant at Egelston Township, Muskegon County, Michigan, co-located with Sun Chemical; USD 2.25 million had been outlaid by July 2026 and the State of Michigan says the award was 'publicly confirmed as retained in May 2026'. Michigan's own support rose from USD 25 million to USD 50 million in August 2026. No revenue, customer or product specification has ever been disclosed; the 2026 website repositions the company as an 'AI-native materials scale-up platform' whose first product is LFP.
ecosystemRole: Mitra Chem sits one layer above every cell maker in this corpus, in the same upstream position as Albemarle on lithium and NOVONIX on anode material: it would sell the LFP cathode active material that a storage cell is built from, not the cell. Its relevance to the AI-data-centre storage buyer is the prohibited-foreign-entity material-assistance test that took effect on 1 January 2026, which makes non-Chinese cathode the binding constraint on a credit-eligible battery — the State of Michigan now describes the Muskegon plant as the first large-scale domestic producer of FEOC-free LFP fully compliant with NDAA supply-chain requirements. That position is prospective: the company has shipped multi-ton samples and named no customer, and the plant that would make it a supplier is unbuilt.

productsAndServices.name: LFP cathode active material (the first product)
productsAndServices.category: Cathode active material — lithium iron phosphate
productsAndServices.description: High-press-density lithium iron phosphate cathode powder for energy-storage and EV cells, developed at the Mountain View facility and produced at multi-ton sample scale on a rented manufacturing line since February 2024. The company's own claim is a 1,000-fold scale-up in two years, from 1 kg per day in the lab to 1,000 kg per day in production, at roughly 20 times lower cost than industry incumbents. A precursor-free synthesis route is described in a company case study as cutting raw-material cost by up to 20% and the product design cycle by 75%. The commercial plant is the 15,000 tonne-per-year Muskegon line, unbuilt as of September 2026.
highlights: Multi-ton LFP samples 'that meet industry-leading electric vehicle specifications' synthesised by February 2024 on a rented line, enabling large-scale customer cell builds and long-term cycling qualification (company)
First commercial-grade LFP samples shipped to 'a tier 1 global battery cell manufacturer' for qualification in September 2022, four months from project start (company)
'Under qualification with top EV and ESS customers' per the 2026 site; no customer has been named on any channel in five years

Muskegon plant: 15,000 t/yr by the original 2027 target, 30,000 t/yr in a second phase; DOE award description: 'ESTABLISH 15 KILO TONNES PER ANNUM (KTPA) OF DOMESTIC MANUFACTURING CAPABILITY OF IRA-COMPLIANT LITHIUM IRON PHOSPHATE (LFP) CATHODE ACTIVE MATERIALS'
State of Michigan (5 August 2026): total investment 'over $370 million', 'up to 150 permanent jobs and 600 construction jobs', 'breaking ground in early 2027, with commissioning in 2028'
Collection gap: no energy density, cycle life, particle size, press-density value or price has ever been published; the case-study charts show axes without values
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Chinese LFP cathode incumbents (Hunan Yuneng, Dynanonic and the rest of a supply that is close to entirely Chinese), Mitra's proposition is provenance and tax-credit eligibility rather than a demonstrated cost or performance lead — the company's '20× lower cost' claim is unsourced and unaudited. Against North American entrants the field has thinned: ICL discontinued its DOE-backed St. Louis LFP plant on 11 November 2025 after DOE withdrew a USD 197 million grant; Nano One runs a pilot at Candiac, Quebec with an 800 t/yr expansion targeted for 2027 and a 25,000 t/yr Canadian plant at concept stage; L&F, Mitra's own 3.3% shareholder, will supply North American ESS customers from a 30,000 t/yr Korean line from 2026, which competes with the Muskegon plant for the same FEOC-free demand it is supposed to serve.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales to cell manufacturers and automotive OEMs; lithium chemicals procured through TechMet-Mercuria as exclusive procurement agent (2023); iron phosphate precursor to be co-produced with Sun Chemical at the Muskegon site.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Muskegon groundbreaking guided to early 2027 and commissioning to 2028 (State of Michigan, August 2026), a year later than the 'early 2026' groundbreaking guided in September 2024 and two years later than the 'commercial production by 2025' guided in 2022; second phase to 30,000 t/yr undated.

productsAndServices.name: The Acceleration Platform and 'The Foundry' (AI-native materials scale-up)
productsAndServices.description: The company's 2026 website reframes Mitra Chem as 'the AI-native materials scale-up platform' and 'an AI-enabled innovator and manufacturer of materials critical for energy, AI, and defense', with LFP as its first product. The platform layers AI agents (named Sparky, Researcher Zero, Swefan and Pierre), specialised machine-learning models, a design studio and data infrastructure over instrumented pilot lines, and is described as deployed 'across the full TRL 3 → 8 workflow'. 'The Foundry' offers shared pilot equipment across chemistries, a process knowledge base and 'AI Super Engineers' to be 'deployed to customer factories', with the best programmes graduating 'into commercial JVs'.
highlights: Company case-study claims: '25× acceleration in identifying failing formulations', '30%' shorter iteration cycles, '100× speedup on data access', '75% time reduction in product design cycle' — all unaudited and undated

Four stated demand drivers on the 2026 site: LFP for Western storage OEMs, hyperscaler power and compute, physical AI and humanoid robotics under rare-earth export controls, and critical-materials reshoring for defense

The 2021 description ('the first North American lithium-ion battery materials product company') and the 2026 description ('scale-up platform… for energy, AI, and defense') are the same company two funding narratives apart
No customer, contract or revenue for platform services has been disclosed
productsAndServices.positioning: This is a services-and-platform framing that widens the addressable story beyond one cathode plant; it competes for attention with materials-informatics companies rather than cathode makers, and nothing in the public record shows it earning revenue.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not disclosed — described as programmes and JVs with 'equipment makers, R&D companies, and chemical majors'.
targetSegments: Defense and AI-hardware supply chains (company framing)

relationships.note: The corpus's other DOE-funded, pre-revenue US battery-materials entrant — synthetic graphite anode in Chattanooga against LFP cathode in Muskegon — occupying the same upstream-materials position on the cell segment.
relationships.context: The two companies do not transact; the link is structural. Both were selected in DOE's Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains battery grant rounds (NOVONIX in 2022, Mitra Chem in September 2024), both have shipped samples without commercial volume, and both sell the FEOC-free provenance that the prohibited-foreign-entity material-assistance test made valuable from 1 January 2026. The contrast is the record: NOVONIX has a built plant with binding offtakes from Panasonic Energy and PowerCo, while Mitra Chem's plant is unbuilt and its customers unnamed. DOE's October 2025 cancellation of Anovion's USD 117 million synthetic-graphite award shows the anode side of this position was not spared by the 2025 reviews either.

relationships.note: LG Energy Solution's Holland, Michigan LFP storage-cell plant, producing since June 2025 and sourcing materials 'from outside China', is the nearest concrete demand for the cathode Muskegon would make; no supply relationship is documented.
relationships.context: Canary Media reported in June 2025 that LGES's 16.5 GWh Holland plant was making LFP cells for stationary storage with battery materials sourced from outside China. Muskegon is about 90 miles from Holland and Mitra Chem's board includes Denise Gray, formerly president of LG Energy Solution Michigan's tech centre. Nothing in either company's record names the other as customer or supplier; the link is proximity and fit, recorded here so the reader does not infer a contract the sources do not contain.

policyExposure.exposure: The prohibited-foreign-entity rules enacted in July 2025 apply a material-assistance cost ratio to projects beginning construction from 2026 — 55% non-PFE content for energy storage under 48E in 2026 rising to 75% after 2029, and 60% rising to 85% for 45X manufacturers — with Treasury's interim guidance in Notice 2026-15 of 12 February 2026. Cells are roughly half of a storage system's equipment cost and cathode is the largest cost inside the cell, so a non-Chinese LFP cathode source is the scarce input the rule creates demand for. Mitra Future Technologies is a US-owned Delaware corporation with US, Korean and Swiss investors and is not a PFE.
policyExposure.mitigation: The State of Michigan describes the Muskegon plant as producing 'Foreign Entity of Concern-free lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material' and 'the first large scale domestic producer of these materials fully compliant with Department of War supply chain requirements included in the National Defense Authorization Act' (5 August 2026).

policyExposure.exposure: Section 45X pays a credit equal to 10% of the production cost of electrode active materials, transferable, with a phase-down for critical minerals from 2031 and the PFE tests applied from 2026. Mitra Chem would qualify once it produces cathode in the United States; until Muskegon is built the credit is prospective.

The State of Michigan's August 2026 release positions the plant's output as 'fully compliant with Department of War supply chain requirements included in the National Defense Authorization Act', and the company's 2026 site lists defense among four demand drivers; In-Q-Tel invested in the 2023 Series B. No defense contract or customer has been disclosed.

The Section 301 rate on Chinese non-EV lithium-ion batteries rose from 7.5% to 25% on 1 January 2026, taking stacked duties on Chinese storage batteries into the 50–58% range, and the 2024 modifications also covered iron phosphate and phosphoric acid. Chinese cathode active material itself has no dedicated AD/CVD case. The tariffs raise the landed cost of the imported cells Muskegon's cathode would displace without touching the cathode powder directly.

Award DEMS0000108 (USD 100 million) was obligated on 16 December 2024, survived the May and October 2025 cancellation rounds that terminated USD 718 million of peer battery awards including ICL's USD 197 million LFP cathode grant, was modified on 13 May 2026, and is described by the State of Michigan as 'publicly confirmed as retained in May 2026'. Only USD 2.25 million had been outlaid by July 2026 and the recorded period of performance ended 30 June 2026 without a visible extension.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that the Muskegon plant is Mitra Chem's project and not L&F's, whatever the Korean headlines say. Basis: the DOE award is obligated to Mitra Future Technologies, Inc. alone with no sub-award; the State of Michigan's 5 August 2026 release names only Mitra as the developer; L&F's own newsroom describes a 3.3% stake and a 'foothold', and L&F told Korean reporters in January and August 2026 that nothing about a US plant is finalized. The 'joint venture' exists in etnews and Newspim, not in any DART filing.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the company has gone quiet on its own channels while its counterparties speak for it, and that this is a risk signal rather than a style. Basis: the last company release is dated 20 September 2024; the 2025 round, the L&F investment, the DOE retention, the doubling of Michigan's support and the 2027–2028 schedule all reached the public through L&F, the State of Michigan, an SEC notice and TechCrunch — which got no reply for comment. A private company whose only near-term catalyst is a groundbreaking, and which has stopped announcing, is one whose status must be re-verified quarterly rather than assumed.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that private capital, not the grant, is the binding constraint on the plant. Basis: the stated cost has moved from 'a $125 million project' (2024) to 'over $370 million' (2026), the award record carries a non-federal share of USD 260.3 million, the 2025 round shows USD 15.6 million sold of USD 50 million with no closing on record, and the state doubled its support to USD 50 million in the same release that pushed groundbreaking to 2027. The grant survived every 2025 review precisely because so little of it had been drawn.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that ICL's exit is a positional advantage only if Muskegon is built, and that the demand ICL judged too weak is the demand Mitra must sell into. Basis: ICL cited DOE's withdrawal, weak EV demand and regulatory change when it cancelled St. Louis on 11 November 2025; the storage side of that demand is real (LGES Holland producing LFP storage cells with non-Chinese materials since June 2025, Ultium Spring Hill converting lines to LFP storage cells in 2026) but no cell maker has named Mitra as a supplier, and L&F will serve the same FEOC-free demand from Korea from 2026 with the Muskegon line as a later option.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the 2026 repositioning from 'battery materials company' to 'AI-native materials scale-up platform' and 'Foundry' is a fundraising narrative built ahead of the plant financing rather than a change in what the company does. Basis: the site now lists hyperscaler compute, humanoid robotics and defense reshoring as demand drivers alongside LFP, and offers shared pilot lines and AI 'super engineers' to customers, with no disclosed platform customer or revenue; LFP remains 'the first product' and the only one with a plant, a grant and a site.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess that GM's role has lapsed from partner to legacy investor. Basis: GM led the 2023 Series B to co-develop LMFP for Ultium, and no GM–Mitra activity, offtake or follow-on has been reported by either party since; the Saint-Gobain Ceramics LMFP manufacturing route promised 'mass production as early as 2026' and has not been mentioned again. Absence of announcement is weak evidence for a company that announces nothing.

**Collection gaps.** No numeric product specification, price or customer name exists on any channel. The Michigan Strategic Fund board memo behind the USD 50 million and the Egelston Township 2026 planning minutes (scanned images) could not be read, so no local land-use approval is evidenced. The DOE award's period of performance ended 30 June 2026 on the public record with no extension visible at the 14 August 2026 update — an inference that it is a budget period, not the project, is stated as such above. The June 2025 Form D lists Chamath Palihapitiya and Jiang-Ling Du as directors while the 2026 board page omits both, and the company has not explained the difference. Headcount is an aggregator figure. sec.gov answered a declared research User-Agent in this session while efts.sec.gov also answered; businesswire.com, woodtv.com, wzzm13.com, michigan.gov and the MSF board-packets page were blocked.

**Indicators to watch.** *Early 2027 — Muskegon groundbreaking:* a ceremony, a township site-plan approval or a DOE NEPA record would confirm Judgment 3's capital gap has been closed; a second slip would indicate it has not. *Any Form D or Form D/A after 9 June 2025:* the 2025 round closing at or near USD 50 million, or a larger round, is the first observable financing event. *A DOE award modification extending the period of performance past 30 June 2026:* absent by mid-2027, the 'retained' status needs re-reading. *A DART filing by L&F naming a US entity, a capital commitment or a stake above 3.3%:* would move Judgment 1 from 'Mitra's project' toward a joint venture. *A named offtake or qualification result from a cell maker (LGES Holland, Ultium Cells, a US integrator):* the first commercial evidence in five years. *Any post on mitrachem.com/news:* the end of the silence recorded in Judgment 2.
